title: Scout C2: orchestrator portability — everything that assumes macOS, this laptop, a TTY or the `f` tool, and what a headless Linux host needs to run Planner-less goals
spec: Read-only scout over /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator (main checkout is on goal/T-0065). Read orchestrator/*.py (spawn.py run_claude and secrets_for_role, executor.py _run, daemon.py notify, pool.py, bus.py state branch mirroring, install.py), .claude/hooks/*.sh (planner-mode.sh temp paths, guardrails.sh, _lib.sh, tests-green.sh), .orchestrator/pool.toml ([secrets.*] commands sourcing f.sh, config_dir paths, codex home), README.md, pyproject.toml. Report: (1) every macOS- or laptop-specific assumption with path:line: osascript/notify, /private/tmp and /var/folders, ~/.claude-a and ~/.claude-b config dirs, ~/.codex, `f tok get` secret commands, uv on PATH, gh CLI, git identity; (2) what a headless Linux host must have installed (claude CLI version pinned in README, codex CLI, uv, node, gh, git) and how each is authenticated non-interactively: read the claude CLI's own help for setup-token or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (run `claude --help` and `claude setup-token --help`; do not run setup-token itself) and codex's for `codex login --with-api-key` or device flow; (3) whether the Planner role is required to run a goal at all, or whether bus_create_task + daemon + spawn can be driven by a script given a plan (i.e. what a start_goal(repo, goal) entry point would call, citing daemon.tick, spawn.run_worker, bus.create_task); (4) how state is kept per target repo (ORCH_ROOT, .orchestrator/, wt/) and what a multi-repo host needs. Cite path:line, one confidence per finding. Do not edit anything.
acceptance: Result lists every host assumption with path:line
Result names the non-interactive auth path for claude and codex CLIs with the command help it read
Result states what a start_goal entry point would call today and what is missing

findings.claim: notify() shells out to macOS osascript for desktop notifications; gated by sys.platform=="darwin" so it silently no-ops on Linux (both-accounts-cooling and budget alerts never reach a human on a headless host).

guardrails.sh's recursive-rm allowlist and planner-mode.sh's allowed_path both hardcode macOS-only temp dirs (/private/tmp, /private/var/folders, /var/folders) alongside /tmp; a Linux host's mktemp under /tmp still passes but the macOS-specific branches are dead weight, and any Linux TMPDIR outside /tmp is only covered via the ${TMPDIR} fallback, which is unset by default.
guardrails.sh's recursive-rm check anchors the only non-tmp allowed target at canon(~/code) — a personal laptop convention for where repos live, not derived from ORCH_ROOT or any config.

Secrets for scout/review roles are fetched by sourcing a personal shell tool (~/.config/f/f.sh) and calling `f tok get <name> --reveal`; f is not part of this repo and protected-paths.txt lists ~/.config/f right next to ~/Library/Keychains, and guardrails.sh separately blocks macOS `security` (Keychain) subcommands — together implying the secrets backend is macOS Keychain via a laptop-only CLI with no documented Linux equivalent.

Phase 0 setup requires an interactive TTY: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-a claude` then the interactive `/login` slash command for each of two accounts, plus interactive `codex login`; none of this is scriptable as written.

`f orch [goal]` is documented as the way to launch the Planner but `f` is an external launcher not present in this repo (found only referenced in README/CLAUDE.md/hooks, never defined here) — a Linux host needs that launcher reproduced or replaced by a direct `claude -p` invocation.

The only container definition in the repo (.devcontainer) is scoped to sandboxing the Codex *executor*, not the Planner/daemon process, and is currently unused because pool.toml sets dangerous_full_access=true (codex runs with sandbox/approvals bypassed on the host directly).

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR itself is not OS-specific and works fine headless once accounts are pre-authenticated; the actual portability gap is in how each account gets authenticated (see next finding), not the env var mechanism.

Non-interactive claude auth path: `claude setup-token` produces a long-lived token (its own --help: "Set up a long-lived authentication token (requires Claude subscription)") meant to back CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; separately, `--bare` mode's help states Anthropic auth in that mode is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper (OAuth/keychain never read) — either path avoids the interactive /login used in README Phase 0. Not run here per task instructions, only its help text was inspected.

open_questions: Is `f` (the ~/.config/f/f.sh launcher and `f tok get` secret command) documented anywhere with a portable/Linux equivalent, or is it purely a personal macOS Keychain wrapper?
Does the Planner's own PR-opening step (CLAUDE.md step 8, `gh pr create`) have any non-interactive gh auth setup expected on a fresh host, or was that always assumed pre-authenticated?
Is there a target git identity (user.name/user.email) meant to be set per-account config_dir, or globally on the host, for commits made by execute-role Claude/Codex workers?
suggested_next: Have a scout trace how `f orch` resolves (search ~/dotfiles or shell rc files referenced by CLAUDE.md) to confirm whether it's reproducible without the personal `f` tool.

Spec a `start_goal(repo, goal)` entry point that: registers ORCH_ROOT per repo (no shared process-global), runs install.py if unscaffolded, and either calls the Planner headlessly via `claude -p --agents ...` with the orchestrate skill, or accepts pre-synthesized specs and drives bus.create_task + daemon.tick directly for complexity<=3 (Claude-free) goals.
Replace notify()'s osascript-only path with a cross-platform hook (webhook/Slack/log line) so headless Linux hosts get the both-accounts-cooling and budget alerts README.md documents.
